lines.text: Ananya asks her college placement bot a simple question: what is my CGPA?
But a language model only writes text. It can't open the college database. Left alone, it would guess.
So your app sends her question together with a menu of tools. Each tool has a name, a description, and the arguments it needs.
The model never sees your Python code. Only this menu.
The model doesn't answer. It replies with a tool call: the function name, get student, and the arguments as JSON.
Notice what did not happen. Nothing has run yet. The model only asked.
Your code parses the arguments, checks them, and runs the real Python function against the database.
Because your code sits in the middle, a wrong roll number becomes a clear error, not a crash.
Then it adds the result to the conversation as a tool message, and calls the model a second time.
Now the model has the facts, so it writes the answer: your CGPA is eight point four.
One question, two API calls. And the model chose that tool using only the description you wrote.
So remember the split: the model proposes, your code executes.
Next lesson: put this in a loop, and you have an agent.
